description:
Advances: specled.api_boundary

Review-bar-override: scoping the block changes what specled.api_boundary.divergence_blocks_refresh currently requires — needs a spec amendment + ADR.

From the critical review of specled_-n5q (finding F29, Medium, consensus: security + api).

has_divergence?/1 is a whole-run boolean applied to a refresh that rewrites every flat tier, so one stuck api_boundary MFA freezes rebaselining for expanded_behavior, typespecs, and use. The attestation path already has the granularity this path lacks — drift_dangling_pairs/1 scopes to subject_id + mfa.

This is consistent with how has_drift?/has_dangling? already behave, so it is not a design objection — the scope is simply undocumented and an adopter debugging a stale unrelated tier will not connect it.

The documentation half LANDED on the release branch (docs/concepts.md now states the block is run-wide and that severity off suppresses the report but not the block). This ticket is the behavioral half only.

## ORCHESTRATOR CONTRACT (specled_-i4x)

Advances: specled.api_boundary

BLOCKED BY specled_-vzd.4. That ticket introduces finding_code/1 + has_code?/2 + the
@drift_code/@dangling_code/@divergence_code attributes and renames drift_dangling_pairs/1. If
this ticket landed first it would write a FIFTH inline `Map.get(f, "code") || Map.get(f, :code)`
copy that vzd.4 then folds in, and vzd.4's rename would land on a function this ticket just
reshaped — a guaranteed same-hunk conflict. After vzd.4, this ticket reduces to an additive
extractor composed from has_code?/2.

DECISION-CLASS: code + spec amendment + ADR, but MERGEABLE after routine review — not held.
The amendment narrows specled.api_boundary.divergence_blocks_refresh
(.spec/specs/api_boundary.spec.md:109-119) and its scenario at :224-233 from run-wide to
per-MFA. change_type: narrows-scope. No weakening class fires (no deletion, no modal downgrade,
no scenario-count drop, no polarity loss), so the weakened-id set is empty and
append_only/same_pr_self_authorization cannot fire. The ADR is required by convention and
specled.decisions.frontmatter_contract, not by a gate.

Allowed touches:
- lib/specled_ex/realization/orchestrator.ex
- .spec/specs/api_boundary.spec.md
- .spec/decisions/specled.decision.*.md  (one new ADR, change_type: narrows-scope)
- test/specled_ex/realization/orchestrator_test.exs
- test/specled_ex/realization/api_boundary_test.exs
- .spec/specs/branch_guard.spec.md  (surface owner of orchestrator.ex, branch_guard.spec.md:24)
- docs/concepts.md AND .spec/specs/package.spec.md — CORRECTION ONLY, and MANDATORY: the
  documentation half of this finding already landed at docs/concepts.md:336-347. If this ticket
  lands, lines 336-341 ("The block spans the whole run, not just the diverged entry") BECOME
  FALSE and must be corrected in the same PR.
- .spec/realization_hashes.json  (escape hatch only)

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/specled_ex/realization/api_boundary.ex
- all other realization modules

Out of Scope (intent):
- Do NOT scope has_drift?/1 or has_dangling?/1 (orchestrator.ex:686-701). They are run-wide by
  design and the ticket says so. The resulting asymmetry (divergence per-MFA, drift run-wide) is
  a deliberate accepted consequence — put it in the ADR's Consequences section, not the diff.
- Do not change what --accept-drift does.
- Do not rename drift_dangling_pairs/1 — that is vzd.4 item 3, which lands before you.
- Do not merge the entry_hash/1 decode duplication (api_boundary.ex:191-201). It is consumed at
  :120 inside the same cond your divergence logic feeds, so it looks adjacent and inviting. It
  is vzd.4 item 1.

PRECISION POINT THE ADR MUST STATE: refresh_and_commit_hashes/3 (orchestrator.ex:897-920) builds
a TIER -> MFA map, while drift_dangling_pairs/1 (:396-414) yields {subject_id, mfa}. The store
has NO subject dimension, so the achievable exclusion granularity is {tier, mfa}, NOT
{subject_id, mfa}. Two subjects binding the same MFA with one diverged means excluded for both.
Say so explicitly; do not claim a granularity the store cannot express.

Verification:
  mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix test test/specled_ex/realization/orchestrator_test.exs test/specled_ex/realization/api_boundary_test.exs
  mix test --only spec:specled.api_boundary.divergence_blocks_refresh
  mix test --only spec:specled.api_boundary.divergence_withholds_drift_silencing
  mix format --check-formatted
  make xref
  bash ./scripts/check_specs.sh
NO stub flip: all four tagged_tests blocks in api_boundary.spec.md are already execute: true,
and orchestrator_test.exs already carries
@tag spec: "specled.api_boundary.divergence_blocks_refresh".

Expected diff: 5-6 files, ~220 lines.

VERIFY: PASS
Session: 9a42db78-611e-4632-882a-adaefdaa666f
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-specled-ex/9a42db78-611e-4632-882a-adaefdaa666f.jsonl

Verified against stage base 0ea3b580..69ff1429 (NOT bb64e69e), judged against contract INTENT since vzd.4 moved the coordinates.

Mechanical checks:
- Files touched: 7 (+212/-56)
- Outside Allowed globs: none. Per-file adjudication:
  - lib/specled_ex/realization/orchestrator.ex — allowed, the ticket's target
  - .spec/specs/api_boundary.spec.md — allowed, the narrowing amendment
  - .spec/decisions/specled.decision.divergence_refresh_scope.md — allowed, the one required ADR
  - test/specled_ex/realization/orchestrator_test.exs — allowed
  - docs/concepts.md — allowed AND mandatory (correction), see below
  - .spec/specs/branch_guard.spec.md — gate-forced surface-owner co-change, NOT creep. orchestrator.ex is branch_guard's declared surface; the edit is the Verification-section "Branch reconciliation note" prose only, replacing the previous branch's stale note. No requirement, scenario or verification block touched.
  - .spec/specs/package.spec.md — same class. docs/concepts.md is package's concepts surface; edit is the reconciliation-note prose only. Requirements untouched.
- Other realization modules untouched: confirmed. `git diff --name-only 0ea3b580..HEAD -- lib/` returns exactly one path, `lib/specled_ex/realization/orchestrator.ex`. api_boundary.ex is absent from the diff, so the entry_hash/1 decode duplication was NOT "helpfully" merged.
- .spec/realization_hashes.json not touched (escape hatch unused). `git status --porcelain` clean at end of verification.

Semantic checks:

- Granularity honesty: HONEST. Neither the ADR nor the amended `must` claims {subject_id, mfa}; both name the store limit explicitly.
  ADR Decision: "The exclusion deliberately cannot be `{subject_id, mfa}`. Two subjects that bind the same MFA share one stored baseline; if either binding diverges, that `{tier, mfa}` entry is excluded for both subjects. Clean-binding attestations remain subject-scoped and continue to exclude the finding's `{subject_id, mfa}` pair."
  Amended must: "Because the hash store has no subject dimension, the baseline shall not be refreshed for any subject sharing the diverged `(tier, mfa)`."
  ADR Consequences repeats it as a cost: "A shared MFA cannot be refreshed for one subject while remaining frozen for another; the store has only one entry to update or preserve."
  Code agrees: diverged_tier_mfas/1 builds MapSet of {tier, mfa} from the finding's "tier"/"mfa" keys; refresh_and_commit_hashes/4 rejects on {Atom.to_string(tier), binding.mfa}. No subject_id anywhere in the exclusion path. The attestation path is unchanged and still keys {subject_id, mfa} via unattested_pairs/1. No overclaim.

- has_drift?/has_dangling? still run-wide: CONFIRMED. Byte-identical to base (base :675-681 vs HEAD :685-691, same bodies, offset only). Neither appears in the diff. The accepted asymmetry is documented in the ADR's Consequences ("Drift and dangling findings remain run-wide refresh gates"), not smuggled into the diff.

- docs/concepts.md corrected and now accurate: CONFIRMED. The false lines 336-341 are gone. New text:
  "**The block is scoped to the diverged tier and MFA.** The affected `api_boundary` entry is excluded from refresh, while unrelated clean entries in `api_boundary`, `expanded_behavior`, `typespecs`, and `use` can still move when the run's other refresh gates permit it. Baselines have no subject dimension, so if two subjects bind the same MFA, a divergence reported for either subject excludes that tier/MFA entry for both."
  The severity-`off` bullet was also updated from "gives you a frozen baseline" to "leaves that entry frozen" — correct, since diverged_tier_mfas/1 reads raw findings pre-severity-resolution. Grepped docs/, api_boundary.spec.md and README for residual "whole run"/"every flat tier"/"run-wide" claims: zero hits.

- Behaviour proved end to end: I built two harness scripts OUTSIDE the repo (scratchpad) and ran the SAME script against a materialized base tree (git archive 0ea3b580 into scratchpad) and against HEAD, reading the WRITTEN .spec/realization_hashes.json after each run via HashStore.read/1.
  Scenario: one api_boundary MFA seeded with resolved_via "source" against a beam-resolving module (forces divergence), a second api_boundary MFA seeded clean but UNLABELED, and a third MFA in expanded_behavior seeded clean with a sentinel key PROBE_STALE_MARKER. A rewrite is observable two ways: the unlabeled api_boundary entry gains resolved_via "beam", and the expanded_behavior sentinel disappears.
  BASE (0ea3b580), normal path AND --accept-drift: diverged entry frozen; clean api_boundary entry has NO resolved_via key; PROBE_STALE_MARKER still present. Whole refresh frozen — the bug.
  HEAD, normal path AND --accept-drift: diverged entry still frozen (hash and resolved_via "source" both preserved, byte-identical to the seed); clean api_boundary sibling now carries resolved_via "beam"; PROBE_STALE_MARKER gone. Unrelated tier refreshed, diverged {tier, mfa} excluded.
  Attestations on HEAD: {:attested_clean, [fetch_entry/3, read/2]} — the diverged MFA is absent, so attestation scoping is unregressed.

- --accept-drift unchanged: CONFIRMED by a 4-cell matrix run identically on base and HEAD, comparing whether the drifted hash was rewritten and whether the other tier's sentinel survived:
  - drift only, no --accept-drift: base {refreshed: false, sentinel survives: true} == HEAD {false, true}
  - drift only, --accept-drift:    base {true, false} == HEAD {true, false}  (self-heal still fires)
  - drift + divergence, no --accept-drift: base {false, true} == HEAD {false, true}
  - drift + divergence, --accept-drift:    base {false, true} == HEAD {false, true}  (run-wide block deliberately retained)
  All four cells identical. The only behavioural delta between base and HEAD is the divergence-without-drift case. Truth-table read of the new predicate confirms this is exhaustive: new `refresh_allowed?` differs from old only when has_divergence? and not has_drift?.
  The retained run-wide block for drift+divergence+--accept-drift is stated in the ADR ("refresh and drift silencing remain withheld together so the command never silences a baseline it did not heal") and in a code comment at orchestrator.ex:206-208. Consistent with specled.api_boundary.divergence_withholds_drift_silencing.

- append_only findings against this diff: NONE. `mix spec.check --no-run-commands --verbose` => `findings=16 (error=0 warning=0 info=16)`, enumerated: 14x branch_guard_missing_subject_update, 2x branch_guard_unmapped_change. Zero `append_only/*`, zero `overlap/*`. Verdict line `spec.check result=pass`. The contract's prediction was RIGHT: no requirement deleted, no modal downgrade (priority stays `must`), scenario count unchanged (the scenario was edited in place, gaining a given and splitting one then into two), no negative/polarity loss. The weakened-id set is empty, so same_pr_self_authorization could not fire. Note the gate ran against origin/main (26 changed files, i.e. vzd.4 + this ticket), so the amendment was definitely in scope of the comparison — most of the 16 info findings belong to vzd.4's files, not this diff.

- Regression test pins per-MFA scoping and reads the written baseline: CONFIRMED BY MUTATION. I copied HEAD into scratchpad, reverted the gate to the base form (`not has_divergence?(findings) and (...)`, exclusion set forced to MapSet.new()), and ran the file. Result: 50 tests, 1 failure —
  "run/2 — divergence scopes baseline refresh a divergence excludes its tier/MFA but refreshes unrelated flat-tier entries" at orchestrator_test.exs:1672, `assert HashStore.fetch_entry(store, "api_boundary", clean_mfa)["resolved_via"] == "beam"` left: nil.
  So it does fail if the exclusion reverts to run-wide. It observes the WRITTEN baseline: every assertion goes through `HashStore.read(root)` after the run, never an in-memory return value, and it re-seeds with `HashStore.write(root, seeded)` before the --accept-drift leg so the second leg is not reading the first leg's residue. The pre-existing non-vacuousness control test at :1718 is untouched and still passes.

- Targeted verification (all in the stage worktree):
  - `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` (MIX_ENV=test) — clean
  - `mix test test/specled_ex/realization/orchestrator_test.exs test/specled_ex/realization/api_boundary_test.exs` — 74 tests, 0 failures
  - `mix test --only spec:specled.api_boundary.divergence_blocks_refresh` — 1 test, 0 failures (exit 0)
  - `mix test --only spec:specled.api_boundary.divergence_withholds_drift_silencing` — 0 tests selected, exit 1. PRE-EXISTING, not caused by this diff: the only test carrying that id is test/integration/drift_acceptance_test.exs:222 under a LIST-valued `@tag spec: [...]`, which ExUnit's `--only tag:value` does not match. I reproduced the identical exit 1 on the base tree at 0ea3b580. This is a defect in the contract's command list, not in the deliverable — specled's own tagged_tests gate does not use `--only`; SpecLedEx.TaggedTests.build_command/2 emits whole FILE paths, so the real gate does execute that test.
  - `mix format --check-formatted` — pass
  - `make xref` — pass (compile-connected at 0)
  - `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` — `validate status=pass errors=0 warnings=0`, `spec.check result=pass`
- Full-suite verification: not run by verifier (by design)

Verdict: PASS

Notes (advisory only, no action required for merge):
1. Same list-tag blind spot applies to the expanded regression test itself: it carries `@tag spec: ["specled.api_boundary.divergence_blocks_refresh", "specled.api_boundary.scenario.divergence_blocks_baseline_refresh"]`, so `--only spec:specled.api_boundary.divergence_blocks_refresh` selects the sibling control test at :1718 instead. Harmless here (the real tagged_tests gate runs the whole file, and the file-scoped run I ran does execute it), but if anyone ever relies on the `--only` selector as the proof of a requirement, it will silently prove the wrong test. Worth a separate ticket on the list-tag/`--only` mismatch rather than a change here.
2. docs/concepts.md still opens the paragraph with the unqualified "it blocks baseline refresh (including `--accept-drift`)" two sentences before the corrected bullet narrows it. Not false in context — the bullet immediately follows and is explicit — but a reader skimming the lead sentence alone gets the old mental model. Cosmetic.
3. The new exclusion silently no-ops if a future divergence finding ever omits "tier" or "mfa" (diverged_tier_mfas/1 guards `is_binary/1` and drops the entry, which would let the diverged baseline be overwritten). Today ApiBoundary always sets both at api_boundary.ex:179-183, so this is not reachable — but it is a fail-open rather than fail-closed shape. Flagging only; no change requested under this ticket.

title: Refresh block is repo-wide, not per-diverged-MFA: one stuck entry freezes every flat tier
